title: The French Revolution
examples: What were the main causes of the French Revolution?
Can you explain the meaning of 'Liberty, Equality, Fraternity'?
How did the period known as The Terror happen?

explain.say: In 1789, France was facing many serious problems.
A key event was the storming of the Bastille fortress.
The revolution promoted the ideas of liberty, equality, and fraternity.
The period called The Terror involved extreme actions against perceived enemies.
In everyday life, times of great change can bring fear and suspicion.
A common mistake is thinking all revolutions are violent.

items: Change can happen slowly over time

faq.q: Why did the French Revolution start?
faq.a: It started due to a mix of social inequality, economic hardship, and Enlightenment ideas challenging the monarchy's power. Asks: What caused the French Revolution? Asks: Why was France unstable?

faq.q: What was the significance of the Bastille?
faq.a: The storming of the Bastille symbolized the people's revolt against royal authority and oppression. Asks: Why is the Bastille important? Asks: What did the Bastille represent?

faq.q: What do liberty, equality, and fraternity mean?
faq.a: These were core ideals meaning freedom for all, equal rights for everyone, and brotherhood among citizens. Asks: What are the French ideals? Asks: Explain the motto.

faq.q: How did The Terror period work?
faq.a: The Terror was a time when the revolutionary government used extreme measures, including mass arrests and executions, against perceived enemies. Asks: What was The Terror? Asks: How did the period end?

faq.q: What was the role of the monarchy before the revolution?
faq.a: The monarchy was the absolute ruling class, believing in the divine right to rule over the people. Asks: Who ruled France before? Asks: What was the old system?

facts: The storming of the Bastille was a major early event.
The guiding ideals were liberty, equality, and fraternity.
The period known as The Terror involved intense political purges.

quiz.say: The storming of the Bastille primarily symbolized:

options.show: The people's revolt against royal power.
options.say: The people's revolt against royal power.

quiz.why: This shows the shift from royal control to popular power.

wrong.0: This is too simple; the event was much larger than just food shortages.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the event was an uprising by the common people.
wrong.3: This is incorrect because the revolution continued for years.

quiz.say: The ideal of equality meant that:

options.show: The king had no power left.
options.say: The king had no power left.

options.show: All citizens were considered equal before the law.
options.say: All citizens were considered equal before the law.

options.show: Everyone could own all the land.
options.say: Everyone could own all the land.

quiz.why: This challenged the old system where status determined rights.

wrong.0: This is the opposite of the revolutionary goal.
wrong.1: While the king's power diminished, equality was a broader legal concept.
wrong.3: While land was an issue, equality was about rights, not just property.

quiz.say: If a government becomes too fearful, it might lead to:

options.show: A period of extreme violence like The Terror.
options.say: A period of extreme violence like The Terror.

quiz.why: Fear allows leaders to justify harsh measures against opponents.

wrong.1: Fear often escalates conflict rather than resolving it.
wrong.2: The Terror was characterized by instability, not stability.
wrong.3: The issues were deeply political and social, not just economic.
